title: Spin disorder competing with positional symmetry breaking governs the metal-insulator behavior in oxide paramagnets
authors: Jia-Xin Xiong, Xiuwen Zhang, Alex Zunger
abstract: Numerous transition-metal oxides have low-temperature antiferromagnetic (AFM) states and high-temperature paramagnetic (PM) phases, where the AFM state is usually insulating while the PM phase can be either insulating or metallic. Without involving strong correlation, we use symmetry-broken density-functional theory (DFT) to obtain the PM phases of insulating NaFeO3 vs the recently discovered metallic NaOsO3. We develop the understanding of insulating and metallic behaviors in paramagnetic oxides by analyzing the interactions between magnetic and positional symmetry breaking: The insulating gap is governed by the competition between the spin disorder that induces a distribution of different magnitudes of local magnetic moments and the polymorphous distribution of off-center atomic displacements. NaFeO3, on the other hand, has large positional displacement with small spin-disorder-induced moments distribution, leading to insulating PM phase, whereas NaOsO3 has a pronounced spin-disorder-induced moments distribution that forces the PM phase to become metallic. Our work identifies this symmetry-breaking competition as a general framework to bridge seemingly disparate metal-insulator behaviors in transition-metal oxides paramagnets without invoking strong correlation.
summary: This work develops a general theoretical framework using symmetry-broken DFT to explain metal-insulator transitions in paramagnetic transition-metal oxides. It shows that the electronic state depends critically on the competition between spin disorder and atomic positional displacements, successfully distinguishing why $	ext{NaFeO}_3$ is insulating while $	ext{NaOsO}_3$ is metallic.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the fundamental physical mechanism governing whether the high-temperature paramagnetic (PM) phase of transition-metal oxide paramagnets is metallic or insulating.
main_result: The metal-insulator behavior in these PM phases is governed by a competition between spin disorder (local moment distribution) and positional symmetry breaking (atomic displacements).
method: Symmetry-broken Density-Functional Theory (DFT) calculations are employed to model the electronic structure of both insulating and metallic states.
model_or_system: The research focuses on transition-metal oxides, specifically comparing $	ext{NaFeO}_3$ (insulating PM phase) and $	ext{NaOsO}_3$ (metallic PM phase). Calculations utilize spin special-quasirandom structures to model disorder without assuming long-range order.
key_observables: Band gap size ($	ext{eV}$), local magnetic moment distribution, and magnitude of off-center atomic displacements ($	ext{\AA}$).
important_parameters: The competition between spin disorder strength and the degree of positional polymorphism is key; strong correlation effects are explicitly avoided.
main_assumptions: The approach avoids invoking strong electronic correlations by using DFT methods that model symmetry breaking via configurational averaging (spin-SQS).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the DOS, showing gap closing for $	ext{NaOsO}_3$ and gap opening/insulating behavior for $	ext{NaFeO}_3$, correlating these changes with moment distributions and atomic displacements.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by contrasting insulating vs. metallic PM phases in oxides. It then develops a general framework based on analyzing how spin disorder interacts with positional symmetry breaking, using DFT calculations on specific examples ($	ext{NaFeO}_3$ vs $	ext{NaOsO}_3$) to validate this competition.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the concept of emergent electronic behavior arising from competing structural/magnetic degrees of freedom (disorder) is relevant to understanding complex quantum many-body systems where multiple order parameters compete.

figures.caption: Figure 1. DFT-calculated projected density of states of PM and AFM phases of (a) NaOsO3 and (b) NaFeO3 that have the orthorhombic crystallographic structures (Pnma). Both AFM phases are insulating, but the PM NaOsO3 is metallic while the PM NaFeO3 is insulating.

Figure 2 shows the distribution of local magnetic moments in PM and AFM phases of NaOsO3 and NaFeO3. Although the net total magnetization is zero, there exists non-zero local magnetic moments in both PM and AFM phases. The distribution of magnetic moments in PM phases cannot be mimicked by the nonmagnetic phases that are often assumed in many works [13– 16,27,28] on transition-metal oxides in the view of strong correlation as the exclusive factor.
